sections.content:
Population change in Wandsworth in 2032

The population in Wandsworth is projected to increase from 329,358 people in 2022 to 357,771 people in 2032.

Despite an overall increase in the population, there is projected to be a fall in net internal migration, which will decrease the population by 28,564 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Wandsworth
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Wandsworth, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 25,145, with 42,404 births and 17,259 deaths in Wandsworth between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Wandsworth by 7.6%, compared with an increase of 6.0% in London and an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 28,564, with 438,813 people moving to the area and 467,376 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Wandsworth by 8.7%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to increase the population by 3,464, with 14,806 people moving to the area and 11,341 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Wandsworth by 1.1%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 27,770, with 81,562 people moving to the area and 53,792 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Wandsworth by 8.4%, compared with an increase of 14.7% in London and an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Wandsworth in 2032

The median age in Wandsworth is projected to remain the same at 33 years between 2022 and 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 11% of the population in Wandsworth are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 9% in 2022.

sections.title: The 20 to 29 age group are set to see the largest change in Wandsworth between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Wandsworth is projected to stay the same, at around 76%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 123 to 129 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Wandsworth?

In 2032, 15% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 19% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Wandsworth between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 6% to 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 7% to 5%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 6% to 5%
